acv.quote: Ninety-five K ACV, on a two-year term.

data.reason: Martin, the CFO, saw only our rate next to the bank's rate. Nothing showed what failed orders cost, so he saw 'the same thing'. Sam blames price, but the value was never shown.

trigger.action: Lead with big orders that fail at checkout, not general acceptance.
trigger.why: Lucy came to us because one in twelve online orders failed, and big baskets failed most.
trigger.quote: about one in twelve online orders was failing at the payment step

decider.action: Put what failed orders cost right next to the rate.
decider.why: Sam never met Martin, the CFO. Martin's page showed only rates and nothing from us on lost orders.
decider.quote: Nothing from us. I assume Lucy told him.

competitor.action: Show the costs a lower rate leaves behind: failed orders, gateway fees.
competitor.why: After the bank cut its rate, Lucy's questions moved from declines to rate. Sam reports this secondhand.
competitor.quote: After the bank came back, every email was the rate.

message.action: Replace the average uplift claim with why big orders get declined.
message.why: Lucy nodded through Farah's big-order decline explanation. The average uplift never became a Fernbrook number.
message.quote: Lucy was nodding the whole way.

proof.action: Add a one-page business case showing what failed orders cost them.
proof.why: Lucy asked for a page for Martin but got the deck. Farah's analysis of their declines was skipped.
proof.quote: something she could hand Martin. Like a one-page business case.

words.action: Say 'orders dying at the last step' instead of 'acceptance rates'.
words.why: Lucy talked about losing a four-thousand-dollar greenhouse sale. Our slide talked about average acceptance.
words.quote: orders dying at the last step
